messages:
emily-devex: Heads-up: a customer reported our 4.3.0 release broke a bunch of onboarding samples running on Bun and Cloudflare Workers. They get: 

emily-devex: `Error: Module not found: Can't resolve '@redwood/sdk/legacy'`

josh-eng: Did we remove subpath/wildcard exports in package.json? We recently tightened the exports map to avoid accidental deep imports.

emily-devex: Yep. package.json now has no wildcard. Current snippet: 

emily-devex: ```json
emily-devex: "exports": {
emily-devex:   ".": { "import": "./dist/index.mjs", "require": "./dist/index.cjs" },
emily-devex:   "./package.json": "./package.json"
emily-devex: }
emily-devex: ```

vlad-runtime: That explains it. Some onboarding samples import internal helpers via `@redwood/sdk/legacy` or `@redwood/sdk/dist/internal`. Removing the wildcard breaks those deep imports. Bun and some bundlers/edge loaders don't tolerate synthetic resolution fallback, so they fail fast.

tina-qa: CI for samples shows tsserver can't resolve types for `@redwood/sdk/legacy` either. TS error: 

emily-devex: ```
emily-devex: error TS2307: Cannot find module '@redwood/sdk/legacy' or its corresponding type declarations.
emily-devex: ```

liza-types: Proposed fixes: 1) Add explicit subpath exports for known public deep imports we want to keep (eg `./legacy`), OR 2) reintroduce a controlled wildcard like "./*": "./dist/*" but documented as internal/unstable. Also add a top-level "types" entry because some toolchains ignore conditional "types" in exports.

josh-eng: Another subtle problem: our SDK used to export a default client construct from the CJS build that wrapped the retry/auth middleware. The ESM entry only exported named factories in 4.3.0. A few sample apps relied on `import SDK from '@redwood/sdk/legacy'` and then `SDK.create()` which gave them an auto-retry wrapper. Now those imports resolve to a light-weight helper without the retry logic, so customers hit auth/retry flakiness in integration tests.

emily-devex: Repro steps I used: 

emily-devex: 1) clone onboarding-samples repo
emily-devex: 2) npm i @redwood/sdk@4.3.0
emily-devex: 3) run sample under Bun: `bun run dev` -> fails resolver

vlad-runtime: Short-term mitigations: publish 4.3.1 that restores explicit `./legacy` subpath pointing to the previous compiled glue file, and add a default export shim on the ESM entry that preserves the old default-created client shape. Also add top-level "types": "dist/index.d.ts" so tsconfig resolution is consistent.

tina-qa: I'll add a test that boots the sample in Bun and Cloudflare Workers in CI, and a TS check. Caught this once already but not for edge runtimes.

liza-types: For long-term, document the public subpaths and mark internal ones as private and unsupported. Too many sample apps depended on internal entrypoints. We should also add a deprecation plan before removing wildcard exports.

build-bot: CI: sample-apps / smoke-tests failed on node 18 + bun + workers (3 failures). Opening an issue with logs.

josh-eng: Good. I'll draft the 4.3.1 patch and a tiny migration guide for customers. Also update onboarding repo to prefer `import { createClient } from '@redwood/sdk'` and avoid deep imports.

emily-devex: Thanks. I'll reach out to the customer with a workaround (pin 4.2.x or change imports) and let them know we're rolling a patch shortly.
